fixes.explanation: Crossing the street and pretending you're busy looking at your phone? Not Paul's plan. He says, "…you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness." (Galatians 6:1). Avoiding him isn't what Paul tells them to do, baker.

That's it, baker. Paul says, "But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted." (Galatians 6:1). The one doing the helping isn't above temptation himself. I'll admit that keeps me humble, because I'm the guy who needs a reminder every time.

Close to how people feel sometimes, friend, but that's not the word Paul uses. He says, "But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted." (Galatians 6:1). His worry is for the helper, who could be tempted too.

Good guess, friend, since Moses, Israel's leader, is who many people think of first when they hear "law." The law came through him (John 1:17). But Paul names a different one: "Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ." (Galatians 6:2). So the answer is Christ's law.

That's right, baker. Paul says, "If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself." (Galatians 6:3). Nobody else even had to be fooled. He did the whole job on his own, like a guy who bakes one batch and sits there convinced he's the best in town.

Close, friend, but it's the other way around. Paul says, "Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else." (Galatians 6:4). The reason to boast is in himself alone, and not in someone else.
